subject.title: [Bug]: Slack Socket Mode ghost connections after gateway restart silently drop inbound messages

question: Should Slack Socket Mode shared-connection handling stay warning-only, or should OpenClaw add a restart-ghost recovery/fencing behavior for stale same-gateway connections?
rationale: Slack documents multiple active Socket Mode connections as a supported deployment pattern, while this issue reports silent message loss from stale restart ghosts; automation cannot choose the compatibility policy or acceptable false-positive risk without maintainer intent and live proof.

options.title: Live-proof scoped recovery
options.body: Require a real Slack restart reproduction, then implement a Slack-plugin-owned recovery that targets stale same-gateway ghosts without breaking documented multi-gateway, relay, or HTTP setups.

options.title: Keep warning-only behavior
options.body: Treat the current diagnostic and docs as the supported policy and keep the operator workaround until stronger evidence justifies automatic intervention.

options.title: Prefer relay or HTTP for production
options.body: Document Socket Mode as single-gateway for production reliability and route multi-gateway reliability to relay mode or HTTP Request URLs instead of adding more Socket Mode policy.

recommendation.title: Live-proof scoped recovery
recommendation.body: Require a real Slack restart reproduction, then implement a Slack-plugin-owned recovery that targets stale same-gateway ghosts without breaking documented multi-gateway, relay, or HTTP setups.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history shows the broadest recent ownership across Slack provider, gateway health, and channel lifecycle paths, making this the best available routing owner for the policy choice.
